title: Biofabrication of Gingival and Alveolar Bone Equivalents: Current Strategies, Advances and Future Directions
html: Purpose of Review Two-dimensional culture models and animal experiments have been used to investigate physiologic and pathologic pathways in oral research. However, these approaches fail to reproduce the structural and cellular complexity of human oral tissues and raise ethical concerns. Consequently, the development of optimized three-dimensional oral tissue models has become essential. Recent Findings This review summarizes recent advancements in the biofabrication of oral tissues in vitro , focusing on gingival and alveolar bone equivalents. The soft-tissue attachment formed around teeth or dental implants acts as a biological seal against bacterial infection, which is the core objective of gingival models. In parallel, engineered alveolar bone models are useful for studying morphogenesis and physiopathological processes. Summary This review highlights current cell sources, extracellular components, and biomaterial scaffolds used to model periodontal and peri-implant diseases. Future developments should integrate immune components, microbial biofilms, and dynamic culture conditions to replicate human oral biology in vitro .
